items.title: Verisk puts Isaias insured losses at $1B-$2B, first industry estimate
items.summary: Catastrophe modeler Verisk issued its initial industry insured-loss estimate for Hurricane Isaias: $1 billion to $2 billion in onshore property losses, covering wind and privately insured storm surge from the Oct 9 Florida Panhandle landfall; wind accounts for the vast majority of losses. Worst wind damage west of the landfall point, in Santa Rosa and northeastern Escambia counties; in Okaloosa County trees falling onto homes was the main damage mechanism. Precipitation-induced flood losses are not expected to be significant. Artemis notes two other early estimates in the same range: Euler ILS Partners $2B-$4B and Cotality $2B-$3B.
